about: Helper messages the format scorer is tested against: four recorded from real walkthroughs, and the shapes the guide forbids, so the scorer's verdicts are pinned rather than assumed.

messages.provenance: Recorded from a live helper run: deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 writing the plan turn's streamed message on the retry-cap fixture (2724 characters). The message is well formed; the helper ended its turn without calling walkthrough_plan.
Recorded from a second live helper run of the same model on the same fixture (2912 characters): three code fences, so it also pins the multi-fence score.

Recorded from a live helper run: gpt-6-luna, the current first pin, writing the plan turn's streamed message on the retry-cap fixture (1736 characters, one code fence). The run planned and committed part 1.
Recorded from a live helper run of gpt-5.6-luna on the same fixture (2283 characters, two code fences): the second pin, and the longest recorded message.
The glm-5.3-flash failure described in docs/latency.md: a Markdown heading inside a part, which the pane renders as a section title the guide forbids.
The other glm-5.3-flash failure: code pointed at with [phrase](src/retry.ts:28) links and no figure fences at all, so the pane shows no code.
A helper that wrote the whole part but not the marker line: the parser finds no content and the commit fails, however good the prose.
A helper that wrapped the message in a :::reply block carried over from the user's thread, which the pane would show as literal markup.
Empty: the tool-only turn, where the helper called the tools with no message at all. Recorded behaviour of Sonnet 5.5 in docs/latency.md, and what a plan turn that never wrote anything scores.
